subject: how-ai-learns
title: How Does a Computer Learn?
summary: Computers can learn from examples, a bit like you learned to spot a dog.

cards.title: Nobody gave you a rule for "dog"
cards.text: How do you know a dog is a dog? Nobody gave you a list of rules. You saw lots of dogs and figured it out. Some computers learn in a similar way.

cards.title: Recipe or examples?
cards.text: Most computer programs follow steps, like a recipe. The computer does exactly what the steps say. But some jobs are too tricky for simple steps, like finding the cat in a photo. For those, computers can learn from examples instead.

cards.title: Learning from labels
cards.text: To teach a computer to spot cats, people show it thousands of pictures. Each picture has a label, like "cat" or "not cat." The computer looks for patterns that match the labels.
cards.example: Spam filters learn this way too. They look at lots of emails that are marked "spam" or "not spam."

cards.title: Turning tiny knobs
cards.text: Inside, the computer has many tiny settings, like volume knobs. At first they are set at random. Each time it guesses wrong, it turns the knobs a little. After lots of practice, its guesses get much better.

cards.title: Smart, but not thinking
cards.text: The Nobel Prize team that explained this work wrote that computers cannot think. They can copy some things brains do, like remembering and learning patterns. A computer can only learn from the examples it is given.

cards.question: If a computer only learned from pictures of big dogs, what might go wrong when it sees a tiny dog? What does that tell us about examples?
nudges: What makes a good set of examples?
Who should check the computer's work?

questions.q: How do some computers learn to spot cats in photos?

options.text: By looking at lots of labeled examples
options.why: Yes! They find patterns in pictures marked "cat" or "not cat."
Words alone would not help it see a cat. It needs picture examples.
Ha! It learns from pictures that people have labeled.

questions.q: What does the computer do when it guesses wrong while learning?

options.text: It adjusts its tiny settings a little.
options.why: Right. Lots of small fixes add up to better guesses.
Wrong guesses are how it learns. It keeps adjusting.
No, it keeps practicing on the examples.

questions.q: Which is true about these learning computers?

options.text: They can only learn from the examples they are given.
options.why: Yes. That is why good, varied examples matter so much.

options.text: They think and feel just like people.
options.why: The Nobel explainer says computers cannot think. They copy some things brains do.
They can make mistakes, especially on things unlike their examples.

cards.prompt: Explain this to someone at dinner in 3 sentences.

sources.title: Popular information: The Nobel Prize in Physics 2024
sources.publisher: The Nobel Prize (Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences)
sources.supports: Traditional software works like a recipe while machine learning learns by example; artificial neural networks inspired by the brain; Hebb's idea that connections strengthen; Hopfield and Hinton; "computers cannot think" but can mimic memory and learning.

sources.title: Explained: Neural networks
sources.supports: Machine learning learns from training examples, often hand-labeled; nodes, weights and thresholds; weights start random and are adjusted in training; 1944 McCulloch and Pitts; the 1957 Perceptron; graphics chips fueled deep learning's return.
